analysis.title: Global Market Outlook: Transitioning to mid-cycle (November 2026)
key_insights: Trims global equities from Overweight to Core (Neutral), leaving the stock-bond mix balanced and gold Overweight. Reasons: US mid-term election volatility, renewed US-Iran strike reports, Brent above USD 110/bbl, high Q3 earnings expectations (especially AI) and higher bond yields.

Caution comes from the risk of an expectations repricing, not from an expected economic slowdown. Debt-financed AI capex is a growing share of total capex (SC estimates 40% of 2027 AI capex is debt-financed).

US and Asia ex-Japan (AxJ) remain Overweight on the highest 2027 earnings growth among major regions. India upgraded to Overweight for non-AI growth diversification, Taiwan stays Overweight, South Korea and China are Core, ASEAN is Underweight.
Japan and Europe ex-UK are Core, with financials as the supporting sector. UK is Underweight for limited exposure to growth sectors.

Bond view: 10Y US yield is in a range last seen in 2007, which improves future return prospects. EM USD government bonds Overweight, DM government bonds Underweight, DM IG and HY corporates Core. Duration limited to 3-7 years.
Core macro scenario is a soft landing (45%), with no-landing upside at 30% and downside at 25%. Recession risk raised to 15% and stagflation probability cut to 10%.

The Fed, ECB and BoJ all hiked in September. SC expects the Fed to hike twice more (December and H1 2027) to a 4.25-4.50% range, the ECB once more in December to 2.75%, and the BoJ to 2.00% by June 2027. Cuts are expected from Q3 2027 for the Fed and ECB.
Money markets price more hawkishness than SC: another 56bps of Fed hikes and more than 60bps of ECB hikes over 12 months.

Gold stays Overweight, with 3m and 12m targets trimmed to USD 4,350/oz and 4,700/oz. Gold is expected to form a base above USD 4,000/oz. USD strength and higher yields are headwinds, offset by EM central bank demand led by China.
Oil: WTI forecasts held at USD 100/bbl (3m) and USD 80/bbl (12m). Freight costs are at multi-year highs, diesel is outpacing crude and inventories are depleting.
DXY 3m forecast raised to 101 from 100.20, 12m held at 98.50. September US payrolls slowed to 29,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2%.
FX forecasts: EUR/USD 1.14 (3m) and 1.17 (12m), USD/JPY 157 and 153, USD/KRW rising to 1,450, USD/CNH falling to 6.52.

Quant stock-bond model score fell to -2 (min -5), signalling a modest equity Underweight and cutting model equity weight to 36% from 68%. Historically this score is associated with flat to slightly negative returns over 3-6 months. Drivers are stretched valuations and weaker technicals.

Short-term regime models show low bear-market probability: 4.2% for the S&P 500 and 7.7% for MSCI AC World, up from 0.9% and 6.4% in September. The US recession model probability is 25% within 6 months, up from 21%.

DM HY spreads have widened to roughly a six-month high. CCC spreads are near a four-year high on AI neocloud funding concerns, which SC views as idiosyncratic. HY all-in yields are above 8%. AI-related IG supply is above USD 250bn in 2026.

Opportunistic ideas: opened US Healthcare (12 Oct) and MSCI Switzerland (29 Oct). Closed Global Semiconductors, MSCI Taiwan, US Communication Services, Global Power & Electrification, EU bank AT1, US utilities hybrids and US 10Y Treasuries. Remaining ideas are US TIPS, AAA CLOs, US HY, AUD corporates, Global High Dividend, Euro area banks and Japan banks.

Sector changes: Europe ex-UK Industrials downgraded to Neutral. US IT, financials, materials and healthcare remain Overweight. The defensive tilt is described as a tactical reduction of tech exposure, not a worse fundamental outlook.
Key event risks: US mid-term elections on 3 November, the US Treasury refunding announcement on 4 November, and Fed and BoE meetings in December.
US data: Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualised, composite PMI is 57.6 and core PCE is 3.1% y/y. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% in October after a September hike.
Brazil: Lula's surprise election win raises political and fiscal risk for LATAM EM bonds. France's fiscal stress is the main risk for the euro and euro area spreads.

earnings_insights: Global equity consensus earnings growth for 2027 is projected at 16% (consensus estimate, not reported). US and AxJ are expected to have the highest 2027 earnings growth among major regions.
US healthcare sector earnings are projected to grow 23% in 2027 (SC projection), the second-fastest among MSCI US sectors.

The US Q3 earnings season is ongoing with high expectations, particularly for AI, which raises the risk of an expectations reset. Europe ex-UK is expected to continue its earnings recovery with Q3 results.

risk_factors: Expectations reset: high earnings expectations combined with higher bond yields and rising debt-financed AI capex.
US mid-term election volatility and policy uncertainty.
Renewed US strikes on Iran and an oil spike, with threats to production infrastructure and depleting diesel inventories.
Central banks accelerating rate hikes, which SC says would push recession risk higher (raised to 15%).
A stock market downturn negating the wealth effect, or a bond sell-off on fiscal concerns.
French fiscal stress and the risk of a euro area spread widening.
AI neocloud funding stress spreading to credit, with CCC spreads near a four-year high.
Private credit spillovers and deteriorating covenant protections.
Brazil fiscal slippage under Lula triggering a LATAM repricing.
El Niño and weather disruptions prolonging inflation in vulnerable EM regions.

vol_and_positioning: Share of equity markets above their 200-day moving averages fell to 47%, from above 80% in August, and below 60% for the first time since January 2025.
Bear market probabilities are 4.2% for the S&P 500 and 7.7% for MSCI AC World, with volatility measures keeping them low.
Investor positioning in US equities and the USD is broadly neutral.
Speculative gold positioning is near May lows, leaving scope for renewed inflows.
The market diversity indicator flags reversal risk in MSCI Europe Real Estate (down over 12% from its August peak) and MSCI China Industrials (down over 19%).
Technical model remains bullish on the S&P 500, with support at 7,607 and 7,493 and resistance at 7,839 and 7,958.
geopolitical: Reports that the US is considering renewed strikes on Iran, with ongoing Middle East conflict keeping oil elevated.
US mid-term elections on 3 November. A Democratic sweep would likely support bonds, while a Republican sweep would likely weigh on them.
French fiscal stress is a risk for the euro and euro area bond spreads.
Lula's surprise win in Brazil's presidential election raises fiscal and political risk for LATAM.
US-Canada trade uncertainty and US trade policy risks affect several regions.
BoJ plans to triple the pace of ETF sales from January 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Exceptional Q3 earnings growth, valuation de-rated from 22x to 19x forward P/E, relative insulation from energy shocks, and 16% global earnings growth expected in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher yields and oil weigh on growth, debt-funded AI capex raises margin bubble risk, and high expectations raise the risk of an expectations reset.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointment in Q3 AI earnings or a bond sell-off after the 3 November mid-term election and 4 November Treasury refunding.

tension_points.bull_case: EM central bank demand led by China, speculative positioning near May lows leaves room for inflows, and a softer USD is expected over 12 months.
tension_points.bear_case: Resilient USD and elevated real yields, with gold-USD negative correlation holding gold back.
